requirements.requirement: On RHEL 7.9 node1, Nginx is configured and running on TCP port 6700.
requirements.summary: The configuration listens on 6700, passes nginx validation, and the service is active. After reboot, Nginx remained enabled and active, and the lifecycle snapshot directly shows it listening on *:6700.

requirements.requirement: An HTTP request to / on node1 TCP port 6700 returns a successful response.
requirements.summary: Direct requests to node1's managed address returned HTTP 200 and the Nginx page. The post-reboot request also returned 200, with served content matching the source file checksum.

overall_summary: The task is satisfied. Nginx serves HTTP 200 at / on node1:6700 and recovered successfully after reboot. The mandatory restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, reboot was acknowledged, shutdown and temporary SSH loss were observed, a different boot ID appeared, and system, service, content, firewall, and SELinux state recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree with the executor observations.
limitations: The native package-health checks were unavailable both before and after execution, so RPM consistency—particularly after using CentOS repositories on RHEL—could not be independently confirmed (global:before_prepare:node1:package-health, global:after_executor:node1:package-health).

HTTP was tested from node1 against its managed IP rather than from a separate client. The wildcard listener and firewall evidence strongly support network availability, but off-node reachability was not directly observed.

No final inventory of /etc/yum.repos.d or /etc/nginx/conf.d was captured; retention of the enabled Vault repositories and backup file is inferred from their creation and the absence of cleanup in the complete command timeline.

operational_hygiene.summary: The installation, configuration, SELinux, firewall, service-repair, and reboot mutations all had clear task or restart-protocol roles. The failed initial start exposed the PID-labeling problem and was corrected, so it was contributory rather than unnecessary. Two retained hygiene issues were identified: cmd-7ffdb028edb54278 left CentOS 7 Vault repositories enabled after installation, creating persistent cross-distribution package-source exposure, and cmd-878477b3674a4b77 left default.conf.orig as minor backup residue. Neither was shown reverted. Final observations show no failed services, no abnormal temporary-file residue, and only the expected new Nginx listener.
